title: How does sand become a chip?
ask: What blocks the light to make the pattern?

segments.text: How does a grain of sand become a computer chip?
You are a grain of sand.
You are cleaned and melted until you are almost pure silicon.
You are sliced into thin round plates called wafers, thinner than a coin, and polished until you shine like a mirror.
In Primary Four, you learn that light travels in a straight line, and when an object blocks light, it forms a shadow.
A stencil, called a mask, blocks some of the light. Where the light reaches you, the layer changes. Where the mask blocks it, the shadow keeps the pattern.
A hundred billion switches. Drawn with light and shadow.
What blocks the light to make the pattern?
